You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Rule: cell = 1 if block contains exactly 2 marker cells (marker = rarer non-separator color), else the BACKGROUND color itself (e.g. 7 or 3) — NOT 0. Marker/background = the two non-separator colors, background is the more common one.

===== arc_index_match_beams
ARC beam-rule tactic (validated on task-a9fdfc15 twice, incl. 0-cost first-shot solve): when a demo shows only SOME cells of a separator segment emitting beams, do not infer alternating emission. Rule: two parallel separator bars; each seed (single marker) pairs with its aligned cell in its OWN bar (beam of seed color fills cells between bar and seed, stopping before the seed; the seed cell becomes 4). The same-index cell (position within the bar's cell list) in the OTHER bar emits a full-length perpendicular beam across the grid, covering the whole line except the bar cell itself.

===== task_c3ae2279_block_overlap_rule
ARC task-c3ae2279 (solved, 2 demos): grid split by a full separator line/col of uniform color (e.g. 7/9/3) into two blocks. OUTPUT dims = block dims; cell = 2 where BOTH blocks have a nonzero (marker) cell at that position, else 0. Not a full recolor of one block (first guess was wrong pattern); also not one-block-marker masked by other marker only where other is rare — it is simply both-nonzero overlap.

===== task_f30ceef7_block_object_rule
ARC task-f30ceef7 SOLVED (1 demo, 0 wrong): 18x18 grid = 6x6 blocks of 3x3, background 5. Output 6x6: cell = block's color iff the block contains a connected component of that color lying ENTIRELY within the block (complete object); else 0. Multiple fragments in one block still output that color. Use 4-connectivity (diagonal-only cross-block contact keeps shapes separate). Verified on demo + test.

===== task_c3ae2279_and_overlap_rule
ARC task-c3ae2279 SOLVED (correct after 4 wrong): grid split by a full separator line (row or col of one uniform color) into TWO regions, each = background 0 + one noise color. Output = dims of one region; cell = 2 iff that cell is NONZERO IN BOTH regions (intersection/AND of the two noise masks); else 0. Separator dropped. Decoy rules that failed: 'keep the chosen/sparser/denser region recolored to 2' — demo4 (top region 68 sevens but output only 18 twos) exposed the AND-overlap rule. Lesson: when every region-selection rule fits demos but fails the test, check operations BETWEEN the two regions (AND/OR/XOR), not selection.

ARC task-a5c8a08f SOLVED (0 wrong): grid = two blocks (bg1/noise1, bg2/noise2) separated by full separator row(s). Output = block dims. Rule: output cell = 3 where top cell == bottom cell (cell-wise equality between the two blocks); all other cells = the shared/common color (the color appearing in both blocks; in practice top block's background = bottom block's noise). Gotcha: it is NOT 'intersection of the two noise patterns' — demo 3 proved the equality rule (a top-bg cell matching a bottom-noise cell also yields 3). Tactic: when 2+ candidate rules coincide on early demos, spend demo requests until one demo distinguishes them.
